The Mask of Fear'' |author=[[Alexander Freed]]{{WebCite|url=https://gizmodo.com/star-wars-reign-of-the-empire-books-alexander-freed-andor-2000480472|text=''Star Wars'' New Book Trilogy Explores the Politics Behind the Rise of the Rebellion|author=James Whitbrook|date=2024-07-29|work=Gizmodo|archivedate=20240729152141}} |cover artist=[[Marko Manev]] |illustrator= |editor=[[Tom Hoeler]] |publisher=[[Random House Worlds]]{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/735101/star-wars-the-mask-of-fear-reign-of-the-empire-by-alexander-freed|text=Star Wars: The Mask of Fear (Reign of the Empire)}} |early release= |release date=[[February 25]], [[2025]] |intl release= |rereleased= |media type=Hardcover |pages=496 |isbn=9780593723463 |isbn2= |isbn3= |audiobook=[[Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear (audiobook)|Audiobook]] |timeline=[[19 BBY]]{{MOFdate}} |series=''[[Star Wars: Reign of the Empire]]'' |preceded by= |followed by=[[Reign of the Empire: Edge of the Abyss|''Edge of the Abyss'']] }} '''''Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear''''' is a novel by [[Alexander Freed]] that was published by [[Random House Worlds]] on [[February 25]], [[2025]]. The novel was codenamed '''Furore''' during development, and was officially announced on [[July 29]], [[2024]]. It is the first novel in the ''[[Star Wars: Reign of the Empire]]'' trilogy. ==Publisher's summary== '''''Before the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebellion]], the [[Galactic Empire|Empire]] reigns, in book one of a [[Star Wars: Reign of the Empire|trilogy]] told through the eyes of [[Mon Mothma]], [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]], and [[Saw Gerrera]].''''' "In order to ensure the security and continuing stability, the [[Galactic Republic|Republic]] will be [[Proclamation of the New Order|reorganized]] into the first Galactic Empire! For a safe and secure society!" ''With one [[Proclamation of the New Order|speech]], and thunderous applause, [[Supreme Chancellor|Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Palpatine]] brought the [[Republic Era|era of the Republic]] crashing down. In its place rose the Galactic Empire. Across [[the galaxy]], people rejoiced and celebrated the end to [[Clone Wars|war]]—and the promises of tomorrow. But that tomorrow was a lie. Instead the [[galaxy]] became twisted by the cruelty and fear of the [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor's]] rule.'' ''During that terrifying first [[Standard year|year]] of tyranny, Mon Mothma, Saw Gerrera, and Bail Organa face the encroaching darkness. One [[Standard day|day]], they will be three architects of the Rebel Alliance. But first, each must find purpose and direction in a changing galaxy, while harboring their own secrets, fears, and hopes for a future that may never come, unless they act.'' ==Development== ===Background=== {{Quote|The Imperial need for control is so desperate because it is so unnatural. Tyranny requires constant effort. It breaks, it leaks. Authority is brittle. Oppression is the mask of fear. Remember that. And know this, the day will come when all these skirmishes and battles, these moments of defiance will have flooded the banks of the Empire's authority and then there will be one too many. One single thing will break the siege. Remember this. Try.|Karis Nemik, in ''Andor''|{{Andor|Rix Road (episode)}}}} ''Mask of Fear'' is part of the wider ''[[Star Wars: Reign of the Empire]]'' trilogy addressing the [[Imperial Era]] and rise of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] over the course of twenty years,{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817940163558830231|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Beginning February 2025 - a new series #StarWars #ReignoftheEmpire. A trilogy charting the rise of the rebellion, across the near 2 decades between Ep 3 and 4. Book 1: The Mask of Fear (Alexander Freed) Book 2 - Rebecca Roanhorse Book 3 - Fran Wilde}} with ''Mask of Fear'' in specific covering{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817946472551186755|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Each book will cover one portion of that near 20 year gap, starting with Book 1 during "Empire Year One" The series will jump forward with each book - we're really taking advantage of the amount of time so each book can be a full complete story (kind of like #HOTD season 1 did)}} a narrow period{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1905405344194458004|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=We're only covering a very narrow spot of time in the first weeks of the Empire. So nothing in this story says they didn't.}} {{C|Padmé was the one holding Mon and Bail together and he knew how she died. But was there a reason why none of them interacted with Queen Apailana or the new senator? Padmé was one of the most influential senators and it's sad that we haven't seen the consequence of her death}} during the first year of Imperial reign, beginning a mere three [[Standard week|weeks]] after the [[Battle of Coruscant]].''[[Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear]]'' As of [[July 21]], [[2025]], the three authors involved for all three books had collectively created over one hundred-thirty pages worth of outlines,{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1947331128286662717|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Fun fact: developing the #StarWars #ReignoftheEmpire series across three books and three authors has generated over 130 pages of outlines combined.}} with most comparable books only creating eight to ten pages as their outlines.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1947331451428425838|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=generally speaking most book outlines (in my experience) are between 8-12 pages, if you need a comparison.}} Those subsequent books in the trilogy jump forward in the timeline to take full advantage of the allotted time frame, presenting the ways in which the galaxy changed over Imperial rule.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/2001386155636371646|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=The time jump creates so many wonderful possibilities, doesn't it? The galaxy is such a different place from where it was in The Mask of Fear. Editorially speaking - we call that a "feature" not a bug.}} [[File:Mothma-Bail-DeletedScene.png|thumb|left|300px|Mon Mothma (left) and Bail Prestor Organa (right) are two major pillars of the ''Reign of the Empire'' trilogy.]] ''The Mask of Fear''{{Threads|darthinternous|post/C-BwvKdOBDU|[[Tom Hoeler]]|date=2024-07-29|quote=A special bedtime story for Intern Lando Our new series announced today. StarWars Reign of the Empire. Beginning this February. Book 1 - The Mask of Fear by Alexander Freed Following Bail Organs, Saw Gerrera, and Mom Mothma during the first year of the Empire. More details here:}} and the wider ''Reign of the Empire'' series{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817950008282341664|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Mon Mothma, Saw Gerrera, and Bail Organa are absolutely our pillar characters, but this series is also going to introduce new and original characters, some who will pass from book to book, and grow / change / evolve across the series.}} follows three "pillar characters," as dubbed by [[Random House Worlds]] editor [[Tom Hoeler]]; these three are [[Senator]] and eventual [[Chancellor (Rebel Alliance)|rebel leader]]{{StoryCite|story=Contingency Plan|book=From a Certain Point of View}} [[Mon Mothma]], Senator and secret early rebel organizer''[[Ahsoka (novel)|Ahsoka]]'' [[Bail Prestor Organa]], and [[Partisans|Partisan]] leader{{TBB|Aftermath (episode)}} [[Saw Gerrera]], himself an early example of someone who offered armed resistance to the Empire. Each appearing across the trilogy in what Hoeler figured would be a fairly equal capacity,{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1818002256945422603|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=All 3 will appear in all 3 books. (fairly equally it appears). But Mon gets the cover treatment here.}} the three each have their own viewpoints that result in them interacting with each other, clashing against themselves, and coming together in what Hoeler promised were "great" ways.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1818005657586696393|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Yeah they represent 3 really interesting viewpoints so having them in each book to play off of / clash with / come together with each other is great. Also they "mark the time" while the original characters are able to really evolve/change in other ways.}} Hoeler further promised that the trilogy would feature new characters, with some of those characters passing between books and growing with each installment. These original characters are able to change and evolve in ways unlike Gerrera, Mothma, and Organa, who all mark the passage of time and can change in their own ways, but who already possess other canonical stories that detail their histories, including fates for Gerrera''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' and Organa.{{StoryCite|story=Eclipse (short story)|book=From a Certain Point of View}} The origins of ''Reign of the Empire'', and with it ''The Mask of Fear'', lied with a desire to tell stories with the same "real" feeling as ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'',{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817945536621650074|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=The entire goal of this trilogy was to tell stories with the same intent / specificity / sense of place & people, and "saying something real" that #Andor does. We want to honor that as best we can. (acknowledging its a bit of a ludicrous and lofty goal)}} a ''Star Wars'' [[Disney+]] series that, in part, features a political perspective on the rebel movement through the eyes of Mothma{{Andor|Aldhani (episode)}} and an on-the-ground perspective through characters like Gerrera.{{Andor|Narkina 5 (episode)}} Initial talks about the Reign of the Empire series started in October 2022, while [[Andor Season 1]] was still airing,{{Substack|subdomain=thecubicleattheendofthegalaxy|url=p/star-wars-reign-of-the-empire-the|text=Star Wars Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear - 100 Things|name=[[Tom Hoeler|Tom]]|username=darthinternous|date=2025-02-11}} and, indeed, the novel is written with fans of ''Andor'' in mind{{BN|url=w/star-wars-alexander-freed/1146072433?ean=9780593723463|text=''Star Wars: The Mask of Fear'' (''Reign of the Empire'')}} and found its title from ''Andor'' dialogue;{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817944119798337697|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=You want more #StarWars #ReignoftheEmpire details? Here's a thread of 'em! First - the book 1 title "THE MASK OF FEAR" (pulpy titles are back!) "Oppression is the Mask of Fear" - Nemik This is not a direct #Andor tie-in (not a Nemik book) but that perfectly captures the tone.}} in ''Andor'', the early rebel [[Karis Nemik]] identifies that "oppression is the mask of fear" in his [[The Trail of Political Consciousness|rebel manifesto]]. All the same, Hoeler has acknowledged that trying to match ''Andor''{{'s}} successes is a lofty goal and noted how the series is not a direct ''Andor'' tie-in, instead explaining that it covers similar ground as ''Andor'' by drawing on the intent and specificity seen in that show. All the same, the team behind ''The Mask of Fear'' nonetheless worked to ensure their work lined up with other ''Star Wars'' stories, as is standard practice for ''Star Wars'' productions,{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1869850804355735597|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Important to remember that these aren't direct ties to Andor, but like any book, we always make sure the stuff we're doing with events, characters, etc. line up with the other Star Wars stories that they overlap with or connect to.}} {{C|In response to: "Did the authors and other people involved get access to any Andor s2 info to make sure everything flowed?"}} and were granted some details about the then-upcoming [[Andor Season 2|''Andor'' Season 2]].{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1889299642774429906|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Some. The book is set many years before even Andor S1 that the events of Andor S2 aren't super critical to building this story. But there's awareness of Andor in general since after all that's part of these characters futures.}} {{C|In response to: "Did you guys/Freed have details on Andor S2 (or even just background ideas/notes) when making this?"}} [[File:SawGerrera19BBY.png|thumb|right|300px|Saw Gerrera (pictured in 19 BBY, around the time frame of ''The Mask of Fear'') is the third pillar of ''The Mask of Fear'' and ''Reign of the Empire'' overall alongside Mothma and Organa.]] Hoeler has further stated that ''Reign of the Empire'' contains looks into the underlying politics of the Imperial Era and questions of how people on the "same side" differ,{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817967720333554045|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Great. Yeah, this definitely has that.}} {{C|In response to: "if this is anything like the aftermath series I'm fully sat and ready to absorb 🧘🏻‍♀️" and "I loved the underlying politics to everything, and the conflicting points of views from people on the "same side" like Mon and Leia - it was a great thinking exercise putting myself in their individual positions"}} a theme also explored in ''Andor''{{Andor|Narkina 5 (episode)}} and other ''Star Wars'' works. According to Hoeler, the trilogy also connects well with Dr. [[Chris Kempshall]]'s then-recent book ''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]''.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817950637352485020|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Chris, your book and this series are like...made for each other.}} {{C|In response to: "It's a very good time for Galactic Empire related content."}} ''Mask of Fear'' is written by the long time ''[[Star Wars]]'' author{{WebCite|url=https://www.alexanderfreed.com/bibliography|text=Bibliography|author=Freed, Alexander|work=[https://www.alexanderfreed.com alexanderfreed.com]|archivedate=20220407063216}} [[Alexander Freed]], who previously has dived into themes of resisting the Empire in works like the rebel-focused novel ''[[Battlefront: Twilight Company]]'',''[[Battlefront: Twilight Company]]'' [[Star Wars: Alphabet Squadron|Alphabet Squadron trilogy]] of novels,[[Alphabet Squadron (novel)|''Alphabet Squadron'']] and the Mothma-focused short story "[[Contingency Plan]]." Hoeler identified "Contingency Plan" as a story for fans to read while they were waiting for ''Mask of Fear''{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817951143407837631|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Think we'll end the thread here...but oh is there so much more to talk about as we get closer to February. In the meantime... Read Alex Freed's Mon Mothma story in From a Certain POV: ANH Read Resistance Reborn by Rebecca Roanhorse Read Fran Wilde's Mon story in FACPOV: ROTJ}} and was very pleased Freed agreed to join the project. The subsequent two novels are written by [[Rebecca Roanhorse]] and [[Fran Wilde]], respectively, who were also returning to the ''Star Wars'' universe with the project.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817947193208123423|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Couldn't be happier about the three authors who agreed to join us in telling these stories. Alexander Freed, Rebecca Roanhorse, Fran Wilde.}} Whereas [[Reign of the Empire: Edge of the Abyss|Roanhorse's novel]] deals more with the rise of the rebellion, ''The Mask of Fear'' depicts the first seeds of revolution as regular citizens ponder how dangerous the times ahead of them are while the Imperial Era begins.{{WebCite|url=https://www.space.com/entertainment/new-star-wars-the-mask-of-fear-novel-stars-mon-mothma-bail-organa-and-saw-gerrera-interview|text='No one really knows that the Emperor is evil': 'Star Wars: The Mask of Fear' author on the early days of the Empire and the birth of the Rebellion (Interview)|author=Jeff Spry|date=2025-02-06|work=Space.com|archivedate=20250614045022}} ===Writing and content=== {{Quote|I'm enormously excited to be a part of this project and explore an era of Star Wars especially rich with the nuanced stories of 'ordinary' citizens—people living inside the machinery of the Empire, still figuring out what's happened to their government and in violent disagreement over ideas of democracy, resistance, revolution, and complicity. It's a chance to write a political thriller and spy drama and sweeping historical epic all at once, as well as spotlight Mon Mothma—a character I've been passionate about for ages. I can only hope the end result does justice to the grand themes of the prequel films, and manages a similar blend of timelessness and relevance.|Alexander Freed, on ''The Mask of Fear''|}} [[File:Alex-Freed.png|thumb|left|250px|Author Alexander Freed (pictured) defines ''The Mask of Fear'' as a political thriller, spy drama, and wide-reaching historical epic all in one.]] According to Freed, ''The Mask of Fear'' is a combination of a political thriller, a spy drama, and a wide-reaching historical epic. Hoeler echoed that sentiment, calling the book something of a political spy thriller, although he did understand comparisons to "''[[Wikipedia:The West Wing|West Wing]]''"-style stories.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817995277250265593|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=It's a little more political spy thriller than West Wing...but I can see what you're getting at.}} According to Hoeler, the novel also deals with themes of grief as the Imperial Era begins.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817984589350252747|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=This is - in part - a book about grief. Grief over the Jedi. The Republic. Padme. His friends lost or gone. Bail is carrying it all, like he does. Because he's Bail, and he wants that burden so others don't have it.}} With the Jedi Order destroyed, the Republic transformed into the Empire, and his comrade and fellow senator [[Padmé Amidala]] dead,{{Film|III}} Senator Organa finds himself carrying the weight of those losses on the hope of taking those burdens from others. Compounding Organa's emotional state is his status as a new father{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817983988499452217|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Look, it's all for Leia. And he's a new dad, and there's a lot of emotions, and he lost his friends, and there's this damn Emperor doing stuff... Its a lot. But Bail's got Breha and they've got Leia. It's gonna be fine. Probably.}} after adopting Amidala's daughter, [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia]]. Trying to do right by her while also dealing with his emotions, his losses, and the actions of the newly anointed [[Galactic Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] creates strife in Organa, who nonetheless has support in Leia and his [[Marriage|wife]], [[Alderaanian monarchy|Queen]] [[Breha Organa]]. ''The Mask of Fear'', like the rest of its trilogy, plays with themes of wealth and privilege thanks to both the backgrounds to some of its cast and the greater story of the galaxy during the Imperial Era.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/2001412461480616197|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Wealth and privilege are always going to be part of this series given the backgrounds of the characters in play, as well as the "goings on" in the galaxy.}} {{C|In response to: Very interested to see how the themes of wealth are to be played with, something you’ve touched on before. In Mask of Fear, Palpatine’s rule is new, so economic elites and corporations are more willing to help Mon since they’re unsure of how this Empire business will pan out. But by Abyss, Palpatine has been in power for years. Those wealthy figures and the corporations have had years to be catered and appealed to. As Amedda tells Mon in Mask, they’re happy to throw *those* people a bone. The idea of corporations and wealthy figures being performatively supportive of democracy but showing they care more about their incentives and profits is… well, relevant is all I can say :P}} According to Freed, at the time the story is set, most people are not yet aware that Palpatine is evil, only that he ended the horrendous Clone Wars, while the image of Jedi was tarnished during the conflict. The novel deals with this period of confusion and uncertainty of which direction the Empire will take. The novel also deals with the [[Delegation of 2,000]] and Amidala's legacy, with the team consulting the deleted Delegation subplot from [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] as a guide.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817948773403726319|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Pulling this one detail out of my #StarWars #ReignoftheEmpire thread. In Book 1 - we are going to dig into some of the content around the Delegation of 2,000/Padme's legacy. And yes we consulted the Ep 3 deleted scenes. (Something many of you have been asking for, for years)}} When discussing his editing work, Hoeler joked that a good portion of the notes his team offered were "just screeching about Mon Mothma."{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817988170493108615|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Half of our editorial notes are just screeching about mon mothma, so you're in good company.}} One line featured within the novel—"All else was shadow"—was stated by Hoeler to be a reference to author [[Wikipedia:J. R. R. Tolkien|J. R. R. Tolkien's]] fantasy writing style.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1850983643520336044|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote="All else was shadow." Love when we can make a little nod to tolkien-esque fantasy language in a Star War. Keeps the fantasy in space fantasy.}} Whether the line made sense in context was a matter of contention during the proofreading process, but the team decided the "vibes" fit the story.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1850984430732787961|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Fun fact - during proofreading we all looked at that line a few times and rightfully noted that, well, that sentence sort of doesn't make much sense. But we all shrugged, agreed the *vibes* are right and kept it in. Sometimes the vibes outweigh everything else.}} One scene between Mothma and the character of [[Lud Marroi]]{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1886434606376718497|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=In three weeks - #ReignoftheEmpire #TheMaskofFear}} was, by Hoeler's reckoning, written at least a year or up to eighteen months before [[February]] [[2025]].{{Bluesky|darthinternous.bsky.social|post/3lhbuxpyozc23|[[Tom Hoeler]]|date=2025-02-03|quote=In case you were curious that page of text was written....at least a year ago, perhaps 18 months.}} Chapter 67 remained largely the same since its appearance in draft one of ''The Mask of Fear'', with only two sentences within changing. One of those changes was to add a non-intrusive reference{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1890048424185352641|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Another chapter that arrived, full formed from draft one. We changed exactly 2 sentences in that chapter. #MaskofFear (One of the changes was to create an amazing deep-cut connection to a different story, that's not intrusive at all, but oh so perfect for anyone who finds it)}} {{C|Quote tweet of: "Chapter 67 of Mask of Fear may be one of the best and most unsettling things I've EVER read, Star Wars and otherwise. Alexander Freed I KNEW you would not let me down"}} that the team was very proud of,{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1890061420731199949|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Let me know if you do! I'm actually wondering how many folks will find it. We're *really* proud of it. Its...*chef's kiss* perfect, and was a very late suggestion by a *very* smart person (not me)}} {{C|In response to: "Gonna go back to the chapter and try and find it 🏃‍♂️💨"}} with Hoeler describing it as a "deep-cut" reference. The reference was added very late into production by someone whom Hoeler described as a "very smart person." The chapter contains a reference to ''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]'': the line "You're an administrator. So ''administrate''" from Mothma to [[Grand Vizier]] [[Mas Amedda]] in the [[2016]] ''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]''{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1904293168084058565|[[Tom Hoeler]]|date=2025-03-24|quote=Chapter 67 ~ #ReignoftheEmpire: The Mask of Fear (2025) - Mas Amedda to Mon Mothma Interlude: Velusia ~ Aftermath: Life Debt (2016) - Mon Mothma to Mas Amedda #StarWars (I love it when a plan comes together)}} by [[Chuck Wendig]], something Hoeler thanked Wendig for writing as a "killer line,"{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1904298863046894010|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=True credit goes to Chuck Wendig for writing a killer line 9 years ago, and it being there waiting for us when we were working on MoF. Once we had the Mas encounter in MoF, someone suggested looking at this LD scene and seeing if there was a "connection" we could make. Perfect}} was recontextualized as something Amedda once says to Mothma in ''The Mask of Fear''. The connection was made when someone on the team suggested going onto ''Life Debt'' to find a connection. According to Hoeler, every time he reads through ''The Mask of Fear'' he has the feeling he will never emotionally recover from its events.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817959405457129859|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Lol I have that same thought every time I finish another read-through of Book 1. Happy to share that burden with everyone come Feb.}} {{C|In response to: "I am simply never going to recover"}} He further described the book's tone by posting lyrics from the [[Wikipedia:Linkin Park|Linkin Park]] song "[[Wikipedia:One More Light (song)|One More Light]]" as if they were sung by Bail Organa{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1828453208928276905|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=🎶Who cares if one more light goes out? In the sky of a million stars It flickers, flickers Who cares when someone's time runs out? If a moment is all we are We're quicker, quicker Who cares if one more light goes out? Well I do🎶- Bail Organa #StarWars #ReignoftheEmpire}} and compared its tone, story, and setting to the well-known opening of{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1831743826484166876|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=A funny thing occurred to me about #ReignoftheEmpire #1 (#TheMaskofFear) and its tone/story/setting. That funny thing: A different #StarWars book has an opener that we *could have* used nearly word-for-word and would have fit pretty seamlessly. Maybe you've read it:}} author [[Matthew Stover]]'s [[2005]] [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|novelization of ''Revenge of the Sith'']],[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]] which Hoeler believed fit very well.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1831743829256335440|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=(Yes I trimmed off the last 2 lines including "twilight of the Jedi" since this book is not that story. Twilight has happened, night has fallen) Otherwise - pitch perfect.}} Hoeler also told a fan who analyzed the Empire's rise to power{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1838677060879028269|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=You just explained a key / essential theme of #ReignoftheEmpire #TheMaskofFear Also, we should get your brother a copy of that book when its comes out.}} as an outgrowth of the Republic's sudden militarization, Palpatine's quick assumption of emergency powers, the suffering inflicted by the Clone Wars, the public's willingness to accept Imperial rule in the name of security due to that war, and the protection granted to the economic elites under the Empire{{Twitter|TheLetterbomber|status/1838675153347354630|Eleanor Mueller|quote=my non-Star Wars fan brother told me, out-of-the-blue, that the Empire's assumption of power makes no sense}} that they had addressed a key theme from ''The Mask of Fear'' and the overall ''Reign of the Empire'' trilogy. [[File:Mothma-GhormanSpeech.png|thumb|right|300px|Mon Mothma stands alone in pushing for change in the Imperial Senate within ''Andor'', a scene that resembles the cover of ''The Mask of Fear''.]] The team behind ''The Mask of Fear'' decided against including a traditional [[Opening crawl|''Star Wars'' opening crawl]], instead beginning the book with two quotes from ''Revenge of the Sith'': Palpatine's proclamation of the Empire and Amidala's sad reflection that the death of liberty has been met with "thunderous applause."{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1846690841861226983|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=In honor of the early drop at #NYCC here's the "intro" for #ReignoftheEmpire #TheMaskofFear. Most SW novels start with a crawl to set the context of the story. We skipped a crawl, because one dialogue pairing from Ep 3 sets up this series better than a crawl ever could.}} Those lines were, in the words of Hoeler, "picture perfect" for ''The Mask of Fear'', although he was unsure if subsequent ''Reign of the Empire'' books would follow that trend.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1846696080685084685|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Not sure if we'll continue them through the series. But for book 1 it was picture perfect}} {{C|In response to: "Oooh I love this. It really sets the tone and makes me curious about which dialogue pairings will be used for the rest of the trilogy."}} The cover of ''The Mask of Fear'' is by artist [[Marko Manev]],{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1817967136599605592|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Forgot one thing (convention brain!) @markomanev created the STUNNING cover for THE MASK OF FEAR. We wanted a cover with a sense of both scene and importantly *scale*. Something to convey the enormity of the Empire, its power, and a sort of sense of loneliness/even grief.}} whose work was intended to depict a quiet sense of isolation,{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1819147897423724719|[[Tom Hoeler]]|quote=Inspiration strikes us from many places. The goal of the cover was to convey a quiet sense of scale (of the Empire) and of isolation. But one of resolution as well. The light is indeed both a beacon in the darkness, but also a spotlight.}} scene, and, quite importantly, the scale of Imperial power. To sell those points, Manev's cover depicts Mothma standing alone in the [[Imperial Senate]], where she is surrounded by other senatorial pods. However, she is the only one to float forward and light up against the room's darkness.
